text: If a Singaporean youth was selected to train and play with Barcelona or Chelsea's youth team, how could the Government support that?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Asians play regularly across European top football leagues not just for their marketing potential but because they have shown that they are good enough.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have faith that a Singaporean playing in one of the top football leagues in the world one day is a possibility and that will certainly put us on the global stage and perhaps do wonders to rejuvenate the sport here.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can the Government do more to perhaps support the Singaporean who finds himself in this position?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My suggestion is let us support more new sports in new and diverse ways that will promote inclusiveness, nurture talent and allow for that collective roar of delight from Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I believe this is not just due to the pride, but also the encouraging notion that one can achieve their dreams as Singaporean in every field, including sports and the arts.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We have a small population, which means a smaller pool where we can select and groom our sports and arts talents from.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Despite the odds, we are glad that our fellow Singaporeans have done us proud in arenas on the global stage.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Currently, how much support is allocated to our local sports and arts heroes?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: How can we enable them to bring out their best?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The past year has seen successes in international sports competitions and arts scene.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Can MCCY further enhance the support system so that local sports and arts talents can continue to achieve their success?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: My second cut on projecting the Singapore culture.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Chairman, Singaporeans learned a lot from documentaries and TV serials from Japan and South Korea.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The Japanese pop (J-pop) and later the Korean pop (K-Pop) groups have significant followings not just among the young but amongst the seniors, too.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I enjoy "Japan Hour" which really whets our appetite by showing us mouth-watering Japanese food.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: It is through such projection of soft power that they subtly exert their influence and project their respective countries' interests.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: It showcases their culture, food and way of life.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Wherever I travel and check into hotels, I will be on the lookout for Channel NewsAsia (CNA) on the hotel TV channels.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I am always happy and feel connected back home just by tuning in to CNA, listening to our own local news.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: CNA is a good example that we should leverage and expand further to showcase and project Singapore culture.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: MCCY should explore and develop more ways and more channels for the projection of Singapore culture to the region and globally.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: This will not only further our national interests abroad but also rally Singaporeans to cherish and preserve our culture.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: In doing so, it will foster a more united and cohesive Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The presence of many startups in one location also helps to build an ecosystem, promote greater creativity and the sharing of ideas.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I would like to offer my take on some concerns on the ground, collated after consultations, and explore strategies for the road ahead.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Our arts and cultural landscape reflect our diversity as a nation.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: There is always something that caters to everyone − traditional to experimental, entertaining works to thought-provoking ones.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is this very diversity that makes the Singapore arts and cultural landscape so exciting and full of vitality which we must strive to encourage.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This is why I feel the need to emphasise the importance of experimental, avant-garde art.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: These are artworks by creators who think out of the box.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: They represent adventure, exploration and offer new ways of seeing, ahead of their time.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, this spirit is not specific to the arts.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We see and celebrate this as well in entrepreneurs, researchers and scientists.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Just like other front-runners, such artworks always meet with hesitation, if not suspicion and derision, by the general public.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, it is common for people to resist the unfamiliar.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, it is the unconventional who bring new knowledge, understanding and change.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As a city state that wants to be at the forefront of innovation, we must embrace artists who have the boldness and imagination to dream extraordinary dreams.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Exploratory works are meant to be contentious, meant to generate critical discourse.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is by grappling with difficult issues that we discover the depth of human thoughts and emotions, understand differences, learn to empathise and celebrate diversity.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The loudest, brashest and most obstinate voices, unfortunately, silenced any possibility of critical discourse.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Precious opportunities for mutual understanding and mediation were lost.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, most of the time, the artists come across as depraved or immoral, with little avenue to express their positions except in their artwork, which may have been banned or censored or which would have only reached out to a small minority of the population.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, how do we deal with sections of the public that promote hate under the guise of moral beliefs?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If an artwork is deemed "objectionable" by one out of 99 people, should that artwork be removed, censored or banned?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I look forward to the day when a representative from the Government will say to an outraged member of the public who wants an artwork banned: if you are offended, do not watch, but there are people who want to watch.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: My point is, we must inculcate in society an appreciation for the value of critical discourse.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We must encourage our people to want to talk about the arts and culture and, to do so, we must understand the value of arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, some may say, how do we value arts and culture when we are still concerned about costs of living?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Valuing the arts means appreciating its intrinsic values.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Arts open up society and shape society, just like we cannot ignore Da Vinci and how we talk about the Renaissance.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: How, therefore, do we help Singaporeans to value arts and culture?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: One of the clearest ways to do this is through arts education.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We need to go beyond simply making students sit through assembly shows or music classes.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: How can we empower our educators to help students see in new refreshing ways and connect arts to life?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We need consistency and rigour in our pedagogical approach to move beyond mere presentation of art and towards seeing art in the everyday.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We are not asking all students to be artists.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But we can find the artists in them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, we need to educate our students on the arts and cultural icons in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In schools, you often see replicas of paintings by Van Gogh and Monet.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But where are our works by Liu Kang, Georgette Chen and Chen Wen Hsi?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If our younger generation cannot access narratives of local artists easily, how can they develop national pride in our arts?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Every child in every school should be familiar with Leong Yoon Pin, Tang Da Wu, Isa Kamari and the list goes on and on.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The history of art must include the critical discourse that is generated from artwork.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: To improve critical discourse, we need to boost research and encourage more critical writing and documentation.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This need to document the arts is especially crucial for our traditional artforms, which we are running against time and need to find new ways to innovate whilst preserving their craft.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But a year on, we have not heard progress on this matter.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Decisions on our cultural assets involve multiple Government agencies and we need to reinforce interagency dialogue and collaboration.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The missteps of Ellison Building and Surviving Syonan Gallery again highlight the importance of good engagement.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I also urge MCCY and the Government to put cultural impact assessments as an important process in forming any major national policy.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Our accomplished artists are recognised nationally yearly through the Young Artists Awards and the Cultural Medallion Awards.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I am too old to receive this now." She is right.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We could have given her the award earlier for her dedication and craft all these years.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: At 86 years old, how would this trophy and grant help her to continue her "artistic pursuits?" How many other older artists have we not heard about, let alone given recognition to?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: There are also other arts workers who have been toiling behind the scenes quietly for decades.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This include TK Sabapathy, art historian and critic, and Tay Tong, producer of TheatreWorks.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, how can these silent heroes and heroines be recognised?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: One of the visions of ACSR is to increase community involvement in art-making, and two very recent cases made me think more deeply about this.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure everyone by now is aware of the Golden Foil Stair at Jalan Rajah, created by La Salle College of the Arts student, Priyageetha.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Some residents have safety concerns about it, but others, including myself, think it is a brilliant piece of art.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In another case, a unique installation of dolls at a void deck, created by a Mr Or, was asked to be dismantled.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, this installation had injected life into that void deck.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In both cases, these installations are in public spaces and they are clear examples of ground-up community art.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Arts in the community is often spontaneous and interventionist, as it should be.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It serves as a response to the place and people around it and engages and enlivens the community in a positive manner.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Should our policies not adjust so as to allow more community engagement and participation in the arts?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Should all agencies and the public not learn how to converse about how to share public space and not mute these ground-up creativity?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Also, should our definition of "community" be inclusive of foreigners in our midst − our migrant workers and domestic helpers − who share our common spaces and actively contribute to our country?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I hope MCCY will consider offering more support to marginalised groups and events, such as the Migrant Workers Poetry Competition and Dibashram, which offers cultural activities to the Bangladeshi community.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We have seen some major shifts in leadership at a few of our largest arts organisations.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Both the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Director of the Singapore Arts Museum left last year.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But to date, no replacements have been announced.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a lack of potential candidates for such leadership roles?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If so, how are we developing new leaders for the future?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Arts institutions need to have artistic leadership at the forefront and should not be driven by just administrative or financial objectives.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As such, I look forward to hearing from MCCY on how it will work with the community to cultivate such leaders, either for future positions at the helm or contributing actively on directorial boards.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I would emphasise that only if these leaders − and I would also include all leaders of other sectors, as well as Government Ministries − embrace arts and culture as essential to our being, then Singapore will move closer to being a liveable and resilient city for a dignified and humanistic being.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: To remain rooted in our Singapore culture that has evolved over many decades, even centuries, let us invest in our heritage so that it binds us together.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Exploring that plate of laksa, lontong, chicken rice or prata can take us through a trek to explore our history.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: We are not just foodies; we connect through food.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Our communal values can be seen in the way we congregate at hawker centres and respect one another's religious dietary habits.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Indeed, one endearing characteristic of many Singaporeans is how we can talk about our favourite food or what we are going to have for our next meal, even as we are eating.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: After all, our local food has gained international recognition through celebrity chefs like Anthony Bourdain and Gordon Ramsay and our kaya kopitiams now dot the region.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: So, let us continue to blog about food and share through community events, traditional and social media and through food fairs.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The musical arts are also an important part of our heritage.
