speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY's work goes to the heart of our nation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: What we do in building "heartware" is often intangible, non-quantifiable.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But there are moments when it becomes clearly evident when everyone feels the same strong emotion deep in our hearts, when we all feel the pulse of our nation's heartbeat.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Across the island, Singaporeans held their breath as they witnessed history being made in a swimming pool halfway across the world.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: From runners at a Charity Run, to football "kakis" meeting up for their regular weekend game, Singaporeans watched the most significant 50.39 seconds in our sporting history.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We proudly "Whatsapp-ed" the photo of our hero to everyone we knew.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Thousands lined the street to welcome Joseph Schooling home and congratulate him, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These moments will be part of our common memory for years to come.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They reflect our national pride and celebrate our common journey.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We saw this at the height of our SG50 celebrations, too, when our Jubilee Weekend peaked at 2015 hours on 9 August with 200,000 gathered around the Marina Bay dressed spontaneously in red and white, or during the SEA Games when Singaporeans sang our National Anthem loudly even when the public address system malfunctioned.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Moments like these affirm the work of MCCY.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The work of MCCY matters more than ever at a time when the world around us is becoming increasingly uncertain.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In developed countries, growing discontent with globalisation has fueled a mood of nativism.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget and COS debates, Members like Dr Tan Wu Meng, Mr Kok Heng Leun, Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, Mr Amrin Amin and Mr Lee Yi Shyan rightly noted that we are witnessing the rise of post-truth politics, where many inhabit echo chambers unwilling to distinguish fact from fiction.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Within our region, the threat of terrorism is on the rise.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Issues of race and religion loom large, with the potential to stoke tensions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Beyond these traditional fault lines, there is a growing risk of rifts along the lines of class, ideology and nationality.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As Dr Lim Wee Kiak pointed out, in these uncertain times, the question facing us is whether we have the social ballast to remain united and resilient in adversity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The strength of our national identity and solidarity will be central to how we fare in a more volatile future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have been described as a small "sampan" in a big ocean.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In turbulent times, when many countries seem to be listing and about to tip, we need steady hands to right the ship and guide it to safety.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Yet, survival and success depend not only on the captain, but on all aboard.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will nurture a caring people, because we need to look out for one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are as strong as the most vulnerable among us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will grow a cohesive society, because a society that stands as one will be able to do difficult things together and overcome the toughest challenges.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And we will build a confident nation, because the courage to dream brought us to where we are today, and the same courage will propel us towards an even brighter future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to grow a civic culture of consideration, care and contribution.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are virtues that Singaporeans can show by caring for one another, their community and their country.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget Debate, Members like Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Tin Pei Ling spoke about the need to grow a spirit of volunteerism.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Henry Kwek hoped to see more citizens volunteering.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development talked about building a community of volunteers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through SG Cares, we can realise a more caring and compassionate society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We may be a small nation, but we can have a big heart.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: She started Keeping Hope Alive, a ground-up initiative of about 60 volunteers that include doctors, plumbers, carpenters, students and families.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Every Sunday, they deliver porridge to residents from over 150 rental flats.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They help the seniors trim their toenails, cut their hair, check for expired food or medication, replace faulty appliances and so on.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These volunteers develop a deep understanding of the needs of the families over time and are able to support them well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The sense of community grows and the circle of caring and giving expands over time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: One volunteer, Ms Siti Nurani Salim, felt so inspired that she started Project Goodwill Aid, reaching out to other needy families in other estates.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is the spirit we hope to cultivate through SG Cares − communities self-organising to care for its members and inspiring others to do good.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For giving to truly make a difference to the lives of people, you need to know well the person you are helping.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is the members of each community who truly understand the needs of their neighbours and friends who are best placed to help make Singapore a truly caring society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SG Cares is a call to all of us to step up to help a neighbour or a cause.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: By linking needs on the ground with the time and talent of volunteers and the resources and capabilities of corporates, we will grow opportunities for volunteerism.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Over time, SG Cares will build capability in organisations to better engage volunteers, equip them with the necessary skills and training, and strengthen volunteer management capacity in our SSOs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That way, we can grow and sustain a vibrant giving landscape.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Joan Pereira reminded us that seniors can be a part of this movement, too.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There are many ways for seniors to volunteer near home.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many of the Pioneer Generation Ambassadors (PGAs), for example, are seniors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: One of them, Mr Wong Phui Sian from my constituency of Yuhua, is one of the most senior PGAs at 75 years young.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Wong has been doing house visits twice a week since he signed up as a PGA in 2015.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He also volunteers at the community garden actively.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The youths of today will be the pioneer generation of tomorrow.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Youth Corps Singapore provides volunteering opportunities for youths from all walks of life to contribute to a more caring Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In partnership with Lakeside Family Services, a group of Youth Corps members developed a financial literacy programme for families living in a transitional shelter.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The young volunteers conducted a series of workshops that taught basic financial knowledge and helped cultivate a habit of saving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, Youth Corps launched its signature programme, "Common Space for Common Good", to bring young volunteers together to serve the community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, we will launch the inaugural Youth Corps Service Week to encourage youths to contribute to social and community causes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Young or old, we can all contribute to issues that concern us and exercise shared responsibility to shape the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have been providing the space and resources for citizens to develop their own ideas.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To encourage more citizens to take the lead in ground-up action, we launched Our Singapore Fund (OSF) to support projects that build national identity or meet social and community needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Joan Pereira asked about the status of OSF.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They range across the arts, heritage, community and volunteerism sectors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Collectively, they supported projects reaching out to over 37,000 people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Wheels@Ubin was a project we supported through the SG50 Celebration Fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In 2015, they brought about 100 wheelchair users to enjoy the sights of Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It involved volunteers from Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT), Changi Sailing Club, the Navy and many VWOs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I met the team recently when they visited MCCY.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Their application for funding under OSF was successful and, this year, they plan to include not just wheelchair users but also the visually impaired.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are happy to see that they are continuing with this meaningful project and are glad to support them again.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Projects like Wheels@Ubin exemplify the Singapore spirit and show how Singaporeans from all walks of life can come together to help one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through OSF, MCCY hopes to encourage more Singaporeans to step forward.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singaporeans also care about how they can play a part in enriching our culture.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our support and funding for the arts and culture will continue to raise arts excellence, grow audiences and ensure that our offerings are accessible to all.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will cater to the emerging needs of the culture sector, whether it is in arts practice, audience development, capability development, or internationalisation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our approach has been to partner the private and people sectors to grow our culture scene together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As of December 2016, over 80 organisations under the cultural sector have benefited from CMF.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope that this top-up will encourage more philanthropy to the sector and provide Singaporeans another avenue to support a cause they care about.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The additional resources enabled SDT to perform in the region, nurture more local choreographers through annual workshops, and reach out to more schools and communities through their arts education programme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: By topping-up the fund, we hope to sustain the momentum of giving to the arts and heritage sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY will take the opportunity to review CMF as part of our regular review of how we fund and support the arts and culture.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY's second focus is enhancing a cohesive society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our future depends on our ability to maintain social cohesion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our multiracial and multicultural identity must be a source of strength and not a cause of fracture.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We may come from different lands and speak different languages.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are proud of our own cultural heritage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our museums, galleries, sports centres and community centres are spaces that bring people of diverse backgrounds together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our religious organisations, youth networks and civil society groups enhance intercultural understanding.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They enlarge our social commons and provide opportunities for Singaporeans to connect and bond.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At a time when tensions are tearing at the fabric of other countries, the bonds and bridges we build in times of peace will enable us to stand together in a crisis.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Alex Yam and Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how we can preserve our social fabric.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We need to partner community leaders and members, and strengthen community vigilance at all levels to absorb shocks and bounce back quickly from any crisis.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We meet apex leaders from major religious and ethnic groups regularly to discuss racial and religious issues on a national platform.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the local level, every constituency has an Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circle (IRCC) that promotes racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We need to take our efforts one step further.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This network will connect with all religious organisations, going beyond the local IRCCs to include those that are not members.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All religious organisations should be plugged into the SGSecure movement, so that they are well-informed and can count on one another for help when the need arises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the hours and days after a terrorist attack, we need respected community and religious leaders to convey messages of calm and solidarity to their congregations and to the wider community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The SGSecure Community Network will prepare our places of worship to be crisis-ready in case of a terrorist attack.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Here is one session where the Roman Catholic Archdiocese shared its crisis plan with the leaders of other faiths.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It reflected the cooperation and trust among the religious organisations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It brought together diverse participants to have frank and respectful discussions on issues of national identity, terrorism and racism over a full day conference.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we have brought the religious leaders together and we have also brought youths of different faiths together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: While Singaporeans support racial and religious diversity, there are still knowledge gaps around religious practices.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Left unaddressed, the knowledge vacuum could be filled by irresponsible voices that seed prejudice.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will deepen religious understanding through in-depth engagements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY will work with community partners to clarify the practice of religion in a multiracial, multi-religious society, and address sensitive questions in a mutually respectful setting.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will also work with community partners to produce content, such as short videos and brochures, which address common, but often unasked, questions on the practices of different faiths.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In Mandarin):   In Singapore, people of different beliefs and races coexist peacefully and look out for one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To preserve our multiculturalism, we must bring religious and racial groups closer together and use the strength of the community to counter terrorism threats.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In line with the SGSecure movement, MCCY is establishing an SGSecure Community Network, to complement IRCC's work on the ground.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The SGSecure Community Network will connect all religious groups, incorporating groups that have yet to join the IRCC.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: After a terrorist attack, these senior leaders of religious and community organisations will be our core mobilisers to convey messages of calm, assuage fear and restore solidarity in the days after.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY will collaborate with religious and community leaders to create more platforms for the public to learn and appreciate the various religious beliefs and practices in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For instance, through the Harmony Fund, we supported the Nanyang Confucian Association's "Confucianism and Islam" seminars, which discussed common values across Confucianism and Islamic theologies and practices.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Such seminars provide valuable platforms for the Chinese community to understand the principle of peace advocated in Islam ideology, and a safe space for discussion to address queries and dispel misconceptions about Islam.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In English): Mr Melvin Yong asked how sports can break down social barriers, promote inclusion and bring communities together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They offer quality programmes at very low cost for young children.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They also bring families and neighbours from all backgrounds together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we launched the Athletics Club, a group of mothers who called themselves "Bedok Mums" requested for such a programme at the Bedok Sports Centre for their children.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: ActiveSG Athletics Club started the programme there and the group of mums and dads meet regularly, twice a week in fact, while accompanying their children.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They share parenting tips on the track side.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: From the photo, we see multiracial, three-generation groupings forming friendship along with their children.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In 2017, ActiveSG will be launching more academies to provide additional pathways for members to engage in and through sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They include traditional sports like badminton and hockey, and non-traditional sports that are gaining popularity, such as frisbee and floorball.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The programmes will cater to different competency levels and provide young adults with both recreational and competitive opportunities to remain active in sports even after leaving the school system.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng will elaborate on this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun asked how we can introduce our students to local artworks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And Ms Sun Xueling asked about co-curating our arts and heritage with students.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Joan Pereira asked about the need to ensure access to arts and heritage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: One way is to expose students to our local arts and heritage scene at an early stage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY is working with MOE to develop more structured student visits to our arts and heritage institutions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At present, some schools already organise visits to our institutions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Some 50% of Primary 5 students have visited the Asian Civilisations Museum (ACM), tapping on exhibits in the museum to complement their Social Studies syllabus.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: By discovering the stories behind the artefacts, students learn about what we inherit from past civilisations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They get to appreciate how history impacts our lives today and develop a habit of learning outside the classroom, beyond textbooks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MOE and NAC are piloting museum-based learning as part of the arts curriculum.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, Primary 4 students from 15 schools visited institutions like the National Gallery Singapore as part of this pilot.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Students from one such school, North Spring Primary, got to understand the history of Singapore through Chua Mia Tee's piece titled "National Language Class".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through this, students learn to appreciate art, the work of Singapore artists and how their art chronicles our shared history.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, NAC will be piloting a Performing Arts-based Learning Programme for lower secondary students, to complement the General Music Programme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Students can look forward to attending a concert by, say, the Singapore Symphony Orchestra.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through this programme, students will learn about concert etiquette and develop a greater appreciation of musical concepts in an orchestral setting.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our aim is for students who have gone through our public school system to have an appreciation for Singaporean artworks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The experiential learning in arts and heritage can become a common reference point for our young, regardless of their background.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope it will be a shared experience that all our students enjoy, and that it will cultivate the audience of the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: OBS is another experience that we hope all Singaporeans will come to share.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, we announced the construction of a new OBS campus on Coney Island as part of our National Outdoor Adventure Education Masterplan.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In January this year, we launched the MOE-OBS Secondary 3 Programme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The new OBS@Coney will stretch the ability of our youths to work together and build resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will combine several schools in one camp to encourage youths to work with peers from different backgrounds.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There will be new features, such as advanced rope courses, that require participants to work in teams.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will also undertake water expeditions around mainland Singapore and learn to respond to challenging scenarios with limited resources.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope that this experience will toughen our youths, create shared memories and forge a more cohesive society for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Seventy five years ago, our Pioneers went through one of the darkest periods of our history.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The fall of Singapore taught us a painful lesson about the importance of national defence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we built up the SAF to safeguard our sovereignty and, this year, we commemorate 50 years of National Service.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Today, we face down the threat of terrorism, tomorrow it might be economic restructuring.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But whatever future challenges might arise, we can overcome them if we have the inner confidence that comes from a strong Singapore Spirit, one that is built on values, such as unity and resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget Debate, Mr Kok Heng Leun described how the arts and culture can build resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Art and music are important parts of what it means to be a well-rounded person and help articulate the voices of a multifaceted society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is why we want Singaporeans to be active participants of the arts and to be proud of our arts and heritage institutions and achievements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our cultural scene has come a long way.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: More Singaporeans recognise the value of arts and culture, and participation in arts and cultural activities has increased across the board.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how we are helping our artists and athletes realise their aspirations and how Singapore is projecting soft power.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The growth of a vibrant arts ecosystem has seen our young artists develop a good international reputation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At 30 years old, he has conducted orchestras in more than 20 cities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is actually the Olympic equivalent for music.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Kah Chun's parents bought him his first trumpet when he was a band member at River Valley High School.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During NS, Kah Chun played the trumpet so often in the SAF Band that he suffered damage to his lips, so he switched to composition and conducting.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Scholarships came from Yong Siew Toh Conservatory, the National Arts Council and the Public Service Commission and allowed Kah Chun to pursue his music education and career, while the Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO) and the Singapore Symphony Orchestra (SSO) gave him opportunities to hone his musical craft.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Despite his achievements, what I really like about Kah Chun is that he has a heart for the community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For the first few weeks, they got to try a variety of instruments and then they will select their own and then, for the last few weeks, they will practise a piece and have a little concert to perform; and the concert is coming soon.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I met one of them at last weekend's session.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Brandvan Yang, the boy who is wearing a cape in the photo, because it was "Superhero Me", so he puts on his superhero cape.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He told me that he loves the violin because it helps him feel relaxed and calm.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He even asked me if I was in a music CCA in school.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It was a moving moment to listen to the children play.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Kah Chun and his friends, all highly talented musicians, are using their gift to inspire Singaporeans who might not otherwise have the opportunity to be exposed to music.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are children from a block of rental flats across the premises, and this little boy who played violin for me actually told me quite proudly that it was "Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star", in minor key.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Similarly, Team Singapore athletes have been great role models to us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Their achievements over the years show we can make our dreams a reality.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to sustain a strong showing at the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games and continue to nurture champions at the Asian and world levels.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Darryl David called for greater efforts to promote sporting excellence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will enhance our High Performance Sports (HPS) system.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I wish to highlight some lessons from our own and other countries' experience at recent major Games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Podium success at world championships and the Olympics requires a focused and sustained effort at all levels.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A talented and dedicated athlete is a necessary starting point.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To groom that athlete into a world champion, we need great coaches supported by deep sports science and sports medicine capabilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Singapore Sports Institute (SSI) and the National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) are critical enablers in this process.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, performance analysts help swimmers improve their performance by providing underwater video feedback on how the swimmers can improve their stroke mechanics.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We must focus on applying science and know-how to help our athletes raise their game.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Another learning point is that success at the elite level requires long-term commitment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Schooling is a two-time Olympian, Pin Xiu and Theresa are three- and four-time Paralympians respectively.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Growing our pipeline of talent and grooming them for podium success require long-term athlete development plans and the resources and technical expertise to create a high-performance training and competition environment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The day-to-day training and competition environment is critical.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will review our HPS system with these principles in mind.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Being a small country without a large population base, we must ensure that resources are used effectively for sustained performance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will require a long-term focus, technically sound training plans and continuity of effort.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our heritage forms an integral part of our national identity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Historical buildings, our urban landscape, our food and festive celebrations, all tell stories of where we come from, who we are today and our legacy for the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Kok Heng Leun asked how we are strengthening our identity and resilience through heritage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have made considerable effort to preserve our heritage assets with the help of the people sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Working with NHB, they have taken the initiative to research and put together heritage trails that bring visitors to landmarks, such as the first Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats at Stirling Road.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To celebrate the civic life of the neighbourhood, "My Community" has been putting up exhibitions to showcase the social history of the area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are not just preserving heritage, they are adding to the richness of cultural life in the community through their own efforts and initiatives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Both surveys are guided by NHB's Heritage Advisory Panel comprising experts from various fields.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Next, we plan to put in place a strategy to document, promote and safeguard our heritage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It will be drawn up in consultation with heritage stakeholders, the public and other Government agencies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng will share more later.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our sporting and cultural heroes are an inspiration because they epitomise the Singapore Spirit.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They show us the importance of having a bold vision, to commit to excellence, determination, a sense of resilience and sacrifice.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are values and ideals exemplified by Mr Lee Kuan Yew and his team who founded independent Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have been actively engaging Singaporeans to co-create a Founders' Memorial that commemorates these values and ideals upon which our nation was built.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singaporeans young and old, expressed strong support for such an effort.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many expressed the hope that the memorial will help current and future generations to cherish and live by such values and ideals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We thank the Committee for leading this community effort.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want Singaporeans to be involved at all stages of conceptualising the Memorial.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will guide the next steps of the design and development.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ultimately, the Memorial will be one for the people, by the people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through courage and diligence, our forefathers forged a nation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through determination and adaptability, they turned challenges into opportunities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With integrity and a commitment to nation-building, they united a people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This tells the extraordinary story of the Singapore Spirit.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When it is ready, the Founders' Memorial will serve that purpose − to continue telling the story.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will be Singaporeans who care for one another, Singaporeans who overcome challenges together, and Singaporeans who dare to dream and are not afraid to pursue our aspirations and our passions for a better Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Minister spoke about our plans to engage more Singaporeans through our arts and heritage offerings.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Singapore's culture scene has, indeed, come a long way.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun spoke about the need to take stock of what has been achieved under ACSR and our plans going forward to 2025.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: More Singaporeans are attending arts events and visiting our museums and heritage institutions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: More Singaporeans also believe in the value of the arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Nevertheless, more can still be done to make culture a part of everyday life and to ensure that culture is inclusive and accessible to all.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to develop and support programmes that can connect with various segments of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok also spoke about involving non-Singaporeans in our arts programmes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the Presentation and Participation Grant, NAC recently supported Kapor ChatParty by The Octopus Residency, a ground-up initiative that aims to foster a sense of community in Little India, whether for residents, patrons or visitors.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As we broaden community outreach and accessibility, we agree with Mr Kok on the value of arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Over the years, we have expanded the space for artistic expression and divergent views.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: At the same time, however, we need to be mindful of our social and cultural context and balance this with mutual respect of views and social harmony.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: While we acknowledge that the arts can be a good platform to teach critical thinking and promote deeper understanding of issues, it is also important for the content and presentation to be context- and age-appropriate.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to work with various stakeholders to bridge this understanding so that we can enlarge the common space for artistic expression and foster a better appreciation of the value of the arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We applaud the work that Mr Kok's theatre company, Drama Box, has undertaken to address sensitive issues, such as race-based tensions, conservation and development through forum theatre, and we hope to learn more from the experience.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC funding guidelines are published and are part of the funding agreement between NAC and the grant applicants.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC seeks to enlarge the space for the arts to flourish without compromising on social cohesion and stability.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We believe that confidence in public institutions is fundamental to the future of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In 2015, Singapore returned to the Venice Biennale.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In 2016, SIFA featured 20 productions, including collaborations between Singaporean and international artists, such as Brian Gothong Tan's Tropical Traumas: A Series of Cinematographic Choreographies, which was presented at Ron Arad's 720° stage at Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will intensify our efforts to raise arts excellence while increasing connection with and accessibility to the arts and, in so doing, help nurture a confident people with pride in their culture and heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We agree with Mr Kok on the importance of making arts a part of our shared spaces and are very encouraged by Priyageetha Dia's creativity to enhance our living spaces.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Understandably, there could be concerns from residents that the local Town Council needs to address.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Hence, we encourage young artists to work closely with the precincts and space managers to enliven our community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One recent example is young artist, Jaxton Su, who worked with the property owner to develop a large-scale mural along Race Course Road which was supported by NAC's Matchbox Grant.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC will be happy to facilitate this process.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok asked for an update on the proposed Traditional Arts Centre.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC worked closely to support all affected arts groups from the Stamford Arts Centre throughout the upgrading process.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Most of the affected arts groups have either moved into other NAC arts spaces or have found spaces through private leases.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The last tenant vacated in end November last year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Since then, NAC has completed a feasibility study and will be starting refurbishment works.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It will bring rich performing traditions closer to the community and support innovative content creation while deepening its relevance in modern Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One idea is to have a residency programme to help seed new collaborations and compelling content.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC also hopes to get the local Waterloo community more involved through the incubation of community arts projects.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Next, I would also like to address Mr Kok's point on developing artistic leadership in our major cultural institutions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We agree that it is important to have these institutions represented by individuals who are passionate about the arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are privileged to have many distinguished arts practitioners sitting on our various boards.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example: Dr Meira Chand, author of the story behind The LKY Musical, serves as a Council Member on the National Arts Council; Mr Gaurav Kripalani, Artistic and Managing Director of the Singapore Repertory Theatre, serves on the board of the National Heritage Board; and Ms Aidli Mohamed Salleh Mosbit, a highly regarded playwright, director, actor, writer, designer and educator and also Young Artist Award winner, serves on the board of the School of the Arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides having a good understanding of the arts and culture, it is important that Board Directors also represent diverse views and offer skills that are fundamental to good governance, such as in audit, finance, legal, audience development and philanthropy.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Chief Executive and Artistic Director oversee the implementation of our cultural policies and set the programming direction.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They are our main interface with the artistic community, patrons and audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They are responsible for stewardship and governance of public resources.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is, therefore, important to identify the right candidate for these key positions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We also agree with Mr Kok that producers play an important role in a vibrant arts and heritage ecosystem by helping our artists put their work out.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides NAC's Creative Producer Development Programme, our cultural institutions like the Esplanade-Theatres on the Bay, also play a role in developing such expertise.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For instance, the Esplanade co-commissions productions and shares risks with producers to develop a canon of Singapore works.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Beyond our shores, the Esplanade and NAC also pave the way for our producers to connect with international markets.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This approach helps to develop a pool of producers who can contribute to art-making both locally and internationally.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As Mr Kok highlighted, our arts and culture landscape today is a product of the legacy of many artistic pioneers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is the amalgamation of efforts of not just artists, but also a wide range of other professionals with creative, management and technical expertise.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We recognise the contributions of these individuals who have been working tirelessly behind the scenes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They can be great mentors to our future generation of cultural professionals.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to look at platforms to recognise them and help them share their expertise with the artistic community as well.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked if it is possible to provide low-cost spaces for artists to showcase their art works or conduct classes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We currently offer a range of long-term housing and short-term rental options at subsidised rates to support our arts sector.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The short-term options, in particular, are flexible and cater to different needs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, the Greenfield Project located at Block O of Goodman Arts Centre offers multi-purpose and project studios with options for rental, either on an hourly, daily or monthly basis.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Beyond Government spaces, we partner the private sector to co-locate arts groups in commercial developments under the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) Community Sports Facilities Scheme (CSFS).

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For instance, Very Special Arts has taken up a space at Changi City Point Mall since 2011.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Given our warm cultural ties with many countries, we have been able to showcase our arts and culture through cultural exchanges and collaborations.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These efforts provide opportunities for our artists to grow.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: At the recent Singapore Art Week, visitors to Gillman Barracks had the chance to observe the artwork in progress when Zai's studio was open to the public then.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As Mr Darryl David highlighted, heritage and culture can build and develop a stronger sense of identity in Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We agree and are working to preserve and promote our heritage in a more comprehensive way.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As the Minister earlier shared, NHB will be developing a comprehensive national blueprint for our heritage sector.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Heritage Plan for Singapore will set out the national vision and action plans for a museum and heritage landscape that will foster a stronger sense of belonging and identity among our people.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One aspect of the Heritage Plan that NHB will be looking at is policy and legislative reviews that will enable us to better conduct the task of archaeology in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This will contribute towards a fuller picture of Singapore's history, going much further than half a century of Independence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the absence of written records, these artefacts provide clues to the kinds of activities that took place on our island.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun spoke about the importance of engaging different segments of society on how our heritage is documented, acknowledged and shared.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Heritage Plan aims to nurture an active community which takes ownership of our heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will seek the views of different groups of stakeholders and different segments of society on a wide range of topics, such as heritage preservation, heritage education and promotion, and making heritage spaces and programmes more accessible and inclusive.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Over the next few months, NHB will continue to hold engagement sessions with heritage stakeholders and partners, including academia, experts, industry practitioners, community and heritage groups, youths, volunteers and educators.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Chairman, NHB and MCCY will be embarking on the important task of inspiring the Singapore Spirit through our diverse cultural heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NHB will be developing a whole new, comprehensive Heritage Plan for Singapore that complements the earlier announced ACSR plans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will gather public feedback and discuss how to systematically document and preserve tangible and intangible heritage, as well as the commonly neglected community heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NHB has already started working on these areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the Heritage Research Grant, academic Dr Koh Keng We conducted research on the local history, rituals, institutions and networks of the Nine Emperor Gods Festival.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: At the same time, NHB also launched a survey on intangible cultural heritage last year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Cultural heritage has always been the microcosm of human development.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Thus, Singaporeans are our best advisors and resources for this blueprint.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides working with the various Government agencies, it is also crucial for NHB to gather ideas from the public through different platforms.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We can then share details of this plan with Singaporeans next year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: From 2018, the plan will guide the long-term development of our cultural heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In this way, we will increase Singaporeans' participation, deepen ownership of our heritage and inspire the Singapore Spirit.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will review this plan every five years, so that it will be a blueprint for Singapore's cultural heritage that truly belongs to us.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: (In English): Beyond arts and heritage, sport is another arena where communities can come together as one.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Complementing the programmes offered by ActiveSG, we will continue to expand and enhance access to sporting spaces through the Sports Facilities Master Plan.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Every year, millions of Singaporeans make use of public sports facilities and the numbers continue to grow.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Melvin Yong spoke about making sports facilities in schools available to the public.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Under the Dual-Use-Scheme (DUS), members of the public can and are making use of facilities like the Indoor Sports Halls and school fields after school hours.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Over the past year, we opened up around 50 more facilities for shared use and are on track to meet our target.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Complementing DUS, the Sports-in-Precinct (SIP) programme also creates accessible play spaces for use by the local community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We initiated a pilot project in Boon Lay.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With the completion of Phase One, residents now enjoy local facilities like the street soccer court and a multi-purpose community lawn court, both laid with an artificial turf.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The street soccer court is well-received and is enjoyed by the youths, who would otherwise usually play on the more common hard court or at the void deck.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides Boon Lay, residents in Jurong Spring can also look forward to similar facilities later this year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: More residents can enjoy playing sports closer to home.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap spoke about hosting national events at the National Stadium.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Singapore Sports Hub was designed to be an integrated sports, entertainment and lifestyle hub for the community and our athletes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is a place where we can enjoy shared experiences and build strong bonds amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Sports Hub Community Play Days and Experience Sports sessions, which are free to the public, have also been organised to encourage more to come and enjoy the offerings at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Nonetheless, more can and should be done by Sports Hub Private Limited (SHPL) to enhance the vibrancy of the Sports Hub and improve the quality of its calendar of events and programming.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These should include major international events, as well as those that the community can participate in.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Minister earlier shared that we will be enhancing our HPS system.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: While SportSG's funding helps NSAs to defray part of their operational costs, NSAs are primarily run, organised and funded by their respective fraternity and need to be accountable to their members for their performance.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Ganesh Rajaram and Mr Faisal Manap spoke about the state of football in Singapore and the role that FAS and its leadership could play to revitalise the football ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We note that the development of Singapore football is currently undergoing a significant transition with FAS due for elections this year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: FAS will need to work closely with its stakeholders, including SportSG, as it develops its multi-year strategic plan.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The plan must address areas, such as youth and coach development, community outreach and participation, and football excellence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We look forward to discussing with the new leadership its future plans for Singapore football and how FAS' plans align with SportSG's Vision 2030.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Ganesh's point about the importance of strong and competent leadership applies not only to FAS but to all NSAs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our NSAs need leaders who can unite their fraternities around a sound strategic plan for the development of their sport.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They must build organisational capabilities that ensure robust governance and effective execution of the strategic plans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They have to invest in and develop professional coaches and officials to help enthusiasts and athletes raise the game.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With strong leadership, good governance, effective management and sound technical capabilities, the sport as a whole can then develop and grow to its full potential.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Henry Kwek has asked about corporate giving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The corporate sector is stepping up, and Deloitte Singapore is a good example.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we hosted the 2015 SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games, Deloitte provided sponsorship and their staff volunteered in creative and marketing support for the Games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As an active member of the spexBusiness Network under SportSG, Deloitte has provided career development opportunities to Team Singapore athletes, such as netballers Charmaine Soh and Kimberly Lim, and recently retired shuttler Derek Wong.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The athletes enjoy a work environment that supports their success in the sporting arena and the workplace.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Deloitte has also partnered NorthLight School to help the students develop their skills and talents through sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And as part of their annual day of service, Deloitte organised a dragon-boat session at the Sports Hub for the students.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We would like more companies to follow Deloitte's lead and give back to society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) launched the Company of Good Programme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The programme helps Singapore-registered companies build capability in giving and connects them with other businesses to champion corporate giving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I agree with Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Ms Joan Pereira that sports and culture must be accessible to all.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, we announced the Disability Sports Master Plan.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Under this plan, we are expanding access for persons with disabilities to take part in sports and developing the organisational and professional capabilities to do so.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SportSG has launched a Centre of Expertise for Disability Sport in Sengkang, with plans to set up at least five such centres in the next few years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It has also offered programmes in swimming, wheelchair rugby, which is held in Toa Payoh, goalball, wheelchair tennis and badminton, and will introduce new ones in football and boccia.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have an Inclusive Gym at the Enabling Village, and there are plans to introduce this at ActiveSG Sports Centres in Bedok, Jurong West, Tampines and Toa Payoh.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will ride on the momentum from the ASEAN Para Games and the Paralympics, and work with partners to raise public awareness for disability sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: One recent collaboration is with four undergraduates from the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) through their final year project, aptly named "Project This Ability".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To promote para-sports as a social activity, they translated the International Symbol of Access into signs that depict wheelchair users playing sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These new signs will be placed at educational institutions, sports centres and Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I attended their Para Sports Day last Saturday at the Enabling Village, where over 230 persons with disabilities, family and friends gathered to try different para-sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: By raising the profile of para-sports and inviting everyone regardless of ability to try, the students are helping to foster an inclusive sporting community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are doing a very good job in introducing para-sports to persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are generating awareness, getting people involved; they are doing a wonderful job for NTU undergraduates.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our cultural institutions are also making their spaces more accessible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The National Gallery has monthly "Gallery Signs" tours, which are led by a docent and a sign language interpreter.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the Singapore Art Museum, many of the works in the annual Imaginarium exhibition can be explored using touch or hearing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This enables visitors with hearing or visual impairment to appreciate the works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, we will strengthen special needs training for museum staff, docents and volunteers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will also be adopting the Picture Exchange Communication System (PECS) to allow persons with disabilities to use picture cards to communicate their needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With regard to Ms Joan Pereira's suggestion to have museums conduct tours in vernacular languages, these are currently available at many of our national museums and heritage institutions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With these developments, everyone can participate more fully in sports and the arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Louis Ng spoke about IPCs that extend overseas to help our neighbours.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are allowed to issue tax deduction receipts on qualifying donations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Hence, there is an expectation that IPCs exclusively help the local community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Where there is an exceptional basis to allow otherwise, the Minister may grant a waiver so that they can conduct overseas activities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This ensures that resources are not collected from the public for overseas causes at the expense of local needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Commissioner of Charities can and does, on a case-by-case basis, waive this rule to support, for example, appeals in aid of providing immediate disaster relief.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Henry Kwek highlighted the challenges that youths face as they enter the workforce and the need for resilience and confidence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We agree that these are important values which cannot be acquired overnight, unfortunately.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are cultivated over time by family, parents and in our schools.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Later experiences at OBS, Youth Corps Singapore and NS reinforce these qualities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Employment aside, youths face other issues when transiting from school to the working world.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about what MCCY is doing to attract overseas Singaporeans to return.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: While the issue of emigration comes under the purview of National Population and Talent Division (NPTD), MCCY's Overseas Singaporean Unit (OSU) keeps in contact with Singaporeans living overseas to maintain their ties back to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We engage them through social media, update them on the latest policy announcements and developments in Singapore, conduct talks with business and Government leaders, and support events which bring Overseas Singaporeans together, such as Singapore Day.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, the Overseas Singaporean Portal offers information to support the relocation journey of overseas Singaporeans customised to their profiles and needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In addition, MOE has a one-stop interface for returning Singaporean students to support their school placement.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For Singaporeans who choose to remain overseas, we hope they continue to fly our flag high, believe in Singapore and find ways to create our nation's future together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The pulse of the nation beats through our arts, heritage, community, sports and youth sectors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At our museums and galleries, we feel that heartbeat.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through the arts and heritage, we celebrate the energy of Singapore's cultural diversity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At our stadiums and sports centres, we feel that heartbeat.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We cheer for our sporting heroes and, like them, we pursue our dreams and reach for the stars.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through OBS, our children feel that heartbeat as they support one another and develop the qualities they need to overcome tomorrow's challenges together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With a strong heart that beats as one, we will build a caring and cohesive society, a confident and resilient nation, and a better home together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarification.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: And I was reminded to say that I also agree that both MCCY and NAC have, over this one year, helped me a lot in terms of bridging a lot of discussions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: First is good news about the arts education and bringing the students to galleries and performances.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I just want to know that through this process, besides disseminating information and knowledge about the art, would there be an interface that allows students to have creative responses to the experience that they had?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think that is the most important part of that art experience.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: That interface requires a lot of thought and good people to work on it.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: How would the Ministry be working on that?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The second thing is the Stamford Arts Centre issue.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: To be honest, during that time, when the tenants were asked to move in a very hurried way, there was quite a lot of unhappiness amongst the group.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think it is not easy for an arts group to move from place to place and that created quite a lot of displacement because there were not very clear plans on how they could move to other places.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Kok, can you please keep your clarifications short?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I hope maybe NAC and MCCY can look into that matter.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The third thing is the Culture Academy which I think it is really very good.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Would this academy create panels as well as discussion possibilities to deal with very difficult, critical discourse issues related to art?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Because if it is attended by a lot of Government officials, that would be very good to start conversations from that point.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Lastly, which is about the staircase, the golden foil staircase.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I want to clarify that this artist has made considerations on the material to be used so that it was not slippery at all.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: However, I think what happened here is that we really probably need to relook at policies, especially dealing with public spaces, especially when such intervention happens.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think this is a very good case for us to look at such issues.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: If you all need, you can come to me and I can bring you on a tour.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We need to find the materials that will have the learning outcomes that meet the needs of MOE.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think we are in the process of having that dialogue and having that pilot project basically to address the issues that the Member has raised.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think that is basic courtesy that the owner should have a right to say yes or no.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When you have raised an issue and raised a proposal, then both parties can sit down and see how to best meet the needs of both parties.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC would learn from this experience because there could be other opportunities or other arts venues that require redesign or redevelopment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We definitely want to prevent such anxiety on the artist/arts group and we will seek to do better.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On the Culture Academy, the Academy regularly invites practitioners and experts from overseas to share their experiences so that our cultural professionals can learn from the best practitioners out there.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Part of that curriculum also include that kind of conversations and to learn from other places which are more advanced in terms of different stakeholder engagements in making decisions on development or in other areas.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: In response to the golden foil, because that is actually a public space.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: How we negotiate public space really needs a lot of more discussions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I do not think I got quite the answer about why Rosa Daniel took up three roles at the same time.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Mind you, again, I said I have no issues with her being in that role, but it is just that one person to take up three roles, are there no other choices that we have?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, to be heading NAC and also as a Deputy Secretary in a Ministry is a heavy task.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Please be assured that we have identified a successor.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is just that, at this point in time, we are not ready for the announcement.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Lim, do you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: On behalf of the Government Parliamentary Committee as well as the colleagues of this House, it remains for me to thank Minister Yaacob, Minister Chan Chun Sing as well as Minister Grace Fu and Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng for their very well-considered response to all our questions, and to all the staff of MCCY as well as related Statutory Boards for their hard work.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We will be there to support them as well.
